title: Automate per-jurisdiction audit sinks and retention via Terraform + Helm upgrades
author: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Private deployments spanning multiple legal jurisdictions require audit exports to be routed to jurisdiction-specific sinks with independent retention and encryption controls. Previously operators performed manual TF + Helm edits and ad-hoc secret rotations during upgrades, which caused configuration drift and intermittent audit delivery gaps.

Solution: This PR adds a dedicated Terraform module (terraform/modules/audit_sink) and Helm values + templates in the audit-log-exporter chart to support conditional routing (by tenant/jurisdiction label), per-sink retention, and automated sink lifecycle management during installer upgrades. The change is designed to be rollout-safe: TF plan is idempotent, Helm changes default to no-op unless operator enables the multisink mode, and the installer upgrade sequence includes a canary path that verifies sink provisioning before switching traffic.

What this PR includes (checklist):
- [x] Terraform module: terraform/modules/audit_sink with resources for GCS/S3/HTTPS sinks, IAM/service-account bindings, and lifecycle rules for retention. Module exposes variables for region, retention_days, kms_key, and tenant_selector.
- [x] Private installer integration: wiring in redwood-private-installer/terraform to call the audit_sink module for tenants with `jurisdiction` metadata.
- [x] Helm chart changes: charts/audit-log-exporter/values.yaml additions (multisink: enabled/disabled, fallback_sink), template changes to render multi-sink routing config, and lifecycle hooks for graceful config swap.
- [x] Upgrade/rollback safety: canary job that validates that newly created sinks accept events before changing the router config; a rollback path that points routers back to the previous sink on failure.
- [x] Secrets handling: secret rotation helper that re-encrypts sink credentials to the cluster KMS and updates Kubernetes secrets via a rolling update to pods.
- [x] Tests & docs: terraform integration tests (local TF plan mocked), Helm linting, and an ops doc describing enablement, required Linear/Jira approvals, and compliance notes.

Notes on config sample (operators will typically set):
  auditExporter: 
    multisink:
      enabled: true
      defaultRetentionDays: 365
      sinks:
        - name: eu-legal-sink
          type: s3
          region: eu-west-1
          retentionDays: 1095
          tenantSelector: "jurisdiction=eu"
        - name: global-archive
          type: gcs
          region: us-central1
          retentionDays: 3650
          tenantSelector: "tenant=*"

Backward compatibility: multisink is opt-in. If multisink.enabled=false (default), the chart behaves like the previous single-sink flow. Terraform module will also no-op unless audit_sink_enabled is set to true in the installer TF variables.

Security & compliance considerations: module requires operators to supply a KMS key per jurisdiction or a key-policy allowing cross-project usage. The PR documents audit expectations and retention mapping requested by Privacy Counsel.

Migration plan: We ship the module behind a feature flag. Early adopter customers will enable in a staging Private deployment and run the included canary job. After successful validation we will enable for broader upgrades via the installer.

References: Linear ENG-4873 (audit-routing), SEC-212 (compliance mapping), internal runbook link: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4873

release_notes: Add optional multi-sink audit export support for Private deployments. Includes Terraform module to provision jurisdictional sinks, Helm chart updates for conditional routing and retention, secret rotation tooling, and upgrade canary/rollback paths. Multisink mode is opt-in behind installer feature flag.
